summary: Independent adversarial release security audit of the ArrTags v1.1 release candidate (branch v1.1, HEAD c7d2a3ad4424ad9de3401795b10ca5b5a37b9b54, artifact artifacts/ArrTags_1.1.0.0.zip 594,931 bytes / SHA-256 85730fe7... / MD5 547beb2f...). The audit covered the ADR-020 logging path and the rewritten SEC-5 (all 21 instrumented log call sites, the IArrTagsLog<T> facade, LogVerbosityGate, LogThrottle, DI wiring, and the task 14.3 live verbosity/secret-scan evidence), the ADR-016 embedded Configuration/config.html page and the elevation-gated Plugin.UpdateConfiguration save path, the ADR-021 configuration-rejection activity-log surface, and release breadth (ADR-005 secret boundary, ADR-012 webhook boundary, state integrity, bounded inputs, packaged artifact). Every prior security finding in docs/implementation/final-review/security-review.json (SEC-1..SEC-9), docs/implementation/9.2, 9.3, 10.3, and 11.1 was reconciled with no regression; the only still-open item is the carried LOW documentation claim at docs/planning/v1.1.md:146-147 (SEC-10.3-2 / P10-F3), which is not a security defect. Verdict PASS_WITH_FINDINGS with 0 open BLOCKER/HIGH. Three accepted hardening limitations are recorded in docs/limitations.md (SEC-10 unbounded configured secret length; SEC-11 unbounded/unvalidated library-scope entries; SEC-12 base-URL user information), all administrator-triggered and none a credential disclosure. No product code, test, build script, or artifact was modified; no commit or tag was created.

Log call-site enumeration at HEAD: 21 IArrTagsLog write sites across the 11 registered categories; every message is a fixed string, a bounded enum/count, a Jellyfin item id, the non-secret normalized connection identity, or a bounded ArrProviderError/sanitized reason; no level-conditional payload expansion; no alternate logging path (no Console/Trace/EventLog/File writers, no custom ILoggerProvider/sink, no host ILoggerFactory replacement).

Independent control-character probe (harness under /tmp/final-review/security/restool): Uri.TryCreate accepts CR/LF in a base URL, but ArrConnectionId normalization escapes them (%0D%0A), so the config-derived connection identity cannot forge a raw log line; the only free-text carriers in log messages are code-owned fixed strings.

Prior-finding reconciliation performed over docs/implementation/final-review/security-review.json, 9.2, 9.3, 10.3, and 11.1 security reviews plus docs/limitations.md SEC-2/SEC-3/SEC-4/SEC-5/SEC-6/SEC-7/SEC-8/SEC-9/SEC-9.3-02; no regression found.

Live evidence cross-checked (not re-run by this task): docs/implementation/14.3/live-verification.json rows L1-L8 all PASS, including L2 (anon page 200; anon configuration GET/POST 401; admin save 204), L5 (exactly one bounded, secret-free activity entry; ArrTags.xml unchanged; no entry on valid save), and L7 (verbosity toggles without restart; 0 secret occurrences in console.log and the log directory).
known_limitations: docs/planning/v1.1.md:146-147 still states the pre-logging 'Current state: The plugin has zero logging call sites' claim (carried from the task 10.3 security review SEC-10.3-2 and the Phase 10 review P10-F3; Phase 13 did not correct it). Exact behaviour: the claim was falsified by task 10.2 and SEC-5 was rewritten by task 10.3, but the planning document still presents it as current state. Precondition: none; it is a documentation-only edit. Consequence: recorded as LOW/open finding SEC-14.4-03 in this review; recommended for correction in the task 14.5 documentation update or a delegated trivial fix. It is not a security defect and does not block the release acceptance criterion (0 open BLOCKER/HIGH).

SEC-10 (new, LOW, accepted): configured provider ApiKey and WebhookSecret strings are not length-bounded, and the anonymous webhook authentication path allocates bytes proportional to the configured secret on each attempt (the untrusted candidate is bounded to 1024 characters). Exact behaviour: requires an administrator to save an implausibly long secret; no default secret; an unconfigured webhook fails closed before any comparison. Consequence: accepted for v1.1 and recorded in docs/limitations.md SEC-10; post-V1 hardening is to bound the configured secret lengths and/or compare lengths before allocating in SecretLease.Matches.

SEC-11 (new, LOW, accepted): EnabledLibraries entries are not count/length-bounded and are not validated as library GUIDs; an entry that is not a GUID is silently ignored and an all-unparseable non-empty scope fails closed for every item (no badges, no error). Exact behaviour: reachable only through the elevation-gated PluginsController save or direct XML editing. Consequence: accepted for v1.1 and recorded in docs/limitations.md SEC-11; post-V1 hardening is to bound the entries and validate the GUID format through the existing rejection path.

SEC-12 (new, INFORMATIONAL, accepted): configured base-URL user information is accepted by validation; ArrTags' own identity and logging exclude it but framework HttpClient logging (outside the plugin verbosity gate) could include the request URI. Exact behaviour: carried from the task 10.3 review SEC-10.3-4; requires an administrator to embed credentials in the URL. Consequence: accepted for v1.1 and recorded in docs/limitations.md SEC-12.

Carried informational residuals, unchanged and re-verified: SEC-2 (shared-temp state-root fallback, LOW open, unreachable on the pinned host), SEC-3 (state-envelope hash does not cover envelope metadata), SEC-4/D1 (generic framework ProblemDetails body on webhook failures), SEC-5's producer-invariant nuance for ArrProviderError.Message/WorkProcessingResult.Reason/MediaMatch.AmbiguityReason (all producers are fixed code-owned strings), SEC-6/D2 (ArtworkSubjectGate process-lifetime bound), SEC-7 (authenticated declared non-JSON content type -> bounded pre-read 400), SEC-8 (no ArrTags-level per-client auth throttling on the anonymous webhook route), SEC-9/SEC-9.3-02 (bounded secret-free activity-log entry; repeated invalid saves can repeat entries by design), SEC-9.3-05/06, and SEC-11.1-1..6. None is a credential exposure or data-integrity loss.

The audit did not start a new live Jellyfin host; the live evidence is the task 14.3 pinned-host matrix cross-checked against the code at HEAD, plus independently re-run default and host-guarded test suites. The Goal B badge-value allowlist remains the one v1.1 surface not exercised live (Phase 14.3 reviewer finding 14.3-R3, disclosed and outside 14.3 traceability); it is covered by unit/integration tests and is not security-relevant beyond its bounded, validated configuration.
docs/limitations.md SEC-2's evidence citation was updated from ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:178-180 to :259-261 because the file grew in v1.1; the finding itself is unchanged.
